name: rapidfuzz_damerau_levenshtein_distance
description: Damerau-Levenshtein distance: like Levenshtein, but swapping two characters counts as one edit, even when other edits occur between them. Returns the distance; 0 means identical. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as n + 1.

name: rapidfuzz_damerau_levenshtein_normalized_distance
description: Damerau-Levenshtein distance: like Levenshtein, but swapping two characters counts as one edit, even when other edits occur between them. Returns the distance scaled from 0 (identical) to 1. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as 1.

name: rapidfuzz_damerau_levenshtein_normalized_similarity
description: Damerau-Levenshtein distance: like Levenshtein, but swapping two characters counts as one edit, even when other edits occur between them. Returns the similarity scaled from 0 to 1 (identical). With `score_cutoff := n`, similarities below n are returned as 0.

name: rapidfuzz_damerau_levenshtein_similarity
description: Damerau-Levenshtein distance: like Levenshtein, but swapping two characters counts as one edit, even when other edits occur between them. Returns the similarity; higher is more similar. With `score_cutoff := n`, similarities below n are returned as 0.

name: rapidfuzz_extract
returnType: STRUCT(choice VARCHAR, score DOUBLE, choice_index BIGINT)[]
description: The best matches for query among choices, best first, like Python's `rapidfuzz.process.extract`. Returns at most `top_k` matches (default 5; NULL for all), each with the choice, its score and its 1-based index in choices. `scorer` names the similarity to rank by (default 'wratio'): any rapidfuzz ratio (e.g. 'ratio', 'token_set_ratio') or a normalized similarity (e.g. 'levenshtein_normalized_similarity', 'jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity'). Choices scoring below `score_cutoff` are skipped, as are NULL choices; ties keep list order.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_extract('new york jets', ['New York Jets', 'New York Giants', 'Dallas Cowboys'], scorer := 'token_sort_ratio', top_k := 2);

name: rapidfuzz_extract_one
returnType: STRUCT(choice VARCHAR, score DOUBLE, choice_index BIGINT)
description: The best match for query among choices, like Python's `rapidfuzz.process.extractOne`: the choice, its score and its 1-based index in choices, or NULL when no choice qualifies. `scorer` names the similarity to rank by (default 'wratio'): any rapidfuzz ratio (e.g. 'ratio', 'token_set_ratio') or a normalized similarity (e.g. 'levenshtein_normalized_similarity', 'jaro_winkler_normalized_similarity'). Choices scoring below `score_cutoff` are skipped, as are NULL choices; ties keep list order.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_extract_one('cowboys', ['New York Jets', 'New York Giants', 'Dallas Cowboys']);

name: rapidfuzz_hamming_distance
description: Hamming distance: the number of positions at which the characters differ. Returns the distance; 0 means identical. Strings of different lengths are compared as if the shorter were padded; with `pad := false` they raise an error instead. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as n + 1.

name: rapidfuzz_levenshtein_distance
description: Levenshtein distance: the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions needed to turn s1 into s2. Returns the distance; 0 means identical. Each kind of edit can be weighted with `insert_cost`, `delete_cost` and `replace_cost` (default 1). With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as n + 1.

name: rapidfuzz_partial_ratio
description: Best `rapidfuzz_ratio` of the shorter string against any equally long substring of the longer one. Useful when one string is a fragment of the other. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!');

name: rapidfuzz_partial_ratio_alignment
returnType: STRUCT(score DOUBLE, s1_start BIGINT, s1_end BIGINT, s2_start BIGINT, s2_end BIGINT)
description: The `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` score together with the substrings of s1 and s2 that produced it. Positions are 0-based character offsets; ranges are half-open.

name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_ratio
description: The higher of `rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio` and `rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio`, computed faster than calling both. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_token_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio
description: `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` applied to the word sets of both strings. Scores 100 when the strings share any word. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_token_set_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'fuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

name: rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio
description: `rapidfuzz_partial_ratio` after sorting the words of both strings. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_partial_token_sort_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

name: rapidfuzz_postfix_distance
description: Postfix similarity: the length of the common suffix of both strings. Returns the distance; 0 means identical. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as n + 1.

name: rapidfuzz_postfix_normalized_distance
description: Postfix similarity: the length of the common suffix of both strings. Returns the distance scaled from 0 (identical) to 1. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as 1.

name: rapidfuzz_postfix_normalized_similarity
description: Postfix similarity: the length of the common suffix of both strings. Returns the similarity scaled from 0 to 1 (identical). With `score_cutoff := n`, similarities below n are returned as 0.

name: rapidfuzz_postfix_similarity
description: Postfix similarity: the length of the common suffix of both strings. Returns the similarity; higher is more similar. With `score_cutoff := n`, similarities below n are returned as 0.

name: rapidfuzz_prefix_distance
description: Prefix similarity: the length of the common prefix of both strings. Returns the distance; 0 means identical. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as n + 1.

name: rapidfuzz_prefix_normalized_distance
description: Prefix similarity: the length of the common prefix of both strings. Returns the distance scaled from 0 (identical) to 1. With `score_cutoff := n`, distances above n are returned as 1.

name: rapidfuzz_prefix_normalized_similarity
description: Prefix similarity: the length of the common prefix of both strings. Returns the similarity scaled from 0 to 1 (identical). With `score_cutoff := n`, similarities below n are returned as 0.

name: rapidfuzz_prefix_similarity
description: Prefix similarity: the length of the common prefix of both strings. Returns the similarity; higher is more similar. With `score_cutoff := n`, similarities below n are returned as 0.

name: rapidfuzz_qratio
description: Like `rapidfuzz_ratio`, but returns 0 when either string is empty, like Python's `rapidfuzz.fuzz.QRatio`. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_qratio('this is a test', 'this is a new test!!!');

name: rapidfuzz_ratio
description: Normalized Indel similarity of the two strings, like Python's `rapidfuzz.fuzz.ratio`. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_ratio('this is a test', 'this is a test!');

name: rapidfuzz_token_ratio
description: The higher of `rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio` and `rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio`, computed faster than calling both. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_token_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

name: rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio
description: Compares the sets of words in both strings, so word order and repeated words are ignored. Scores 100 when the words of one string are a subset of the other. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_token_set_ratio('fuzzy was a bear', 'fuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

name: rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio
description: `rapidfuzz_ratio` after splitting both strings on whitespace and sorting the words, so word order is ignored. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_token_sort_ratio('fuzzy wuzzy was a bear', 'wuzzy fuzzy was a bear');

name: rapidfuzz_wratio
description: Weighted combination of the ratio, partial and token scorers chosen by the strings' length ratio, like Python's `rapidfuzz.fuzz.WRatio`. A good general-purpose default. Returns a score from 0 to 100. With `score_cutoff := n`, scores below n are returned as 0.

examples.code: SELECT rapidfuzz_wratio('this is a test', 'this is a new test!!!');
